title: Python: from m import f; f() refuses where m.f() gives x.g, for an aliased hop through a star-only module (GCLI-124 round 2 note 1)
description: Found in the GCLI-124 Opus round 2 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#201, landed 3871e4d5): a LOST edge, not a wrong one. Input: x.py has def g and def f; n.py is 'from x import *'; m.py is 'from n import g as f'; app.py is 'from m import f' then 'f()'. Since #201 the from-import form gives NO edge (it was the WRONG edge x.f, where Python binds x.g); the attribute form 'import m; m.f()' gives x.g correctly. Cause: resolveImportBinding calls sourceChainOutcome with refuseRenamed, so a walk that renamed the name (f to g) and dead-ends at a star-only module is a refusal. A fix would give the from-import path resolveModuleAttribute's recursion on the imported name (resolveModuleAttribute(binding.target, importedName) after the walk), which already returns x.g. Same dead end for the unconditional twin and for (b) 'from . import g as f' (binds a module, so no edge is right there) and (c) plain-import hop (module, no edge is right): only (a) loses a correct edge. Reviewer note 2: the parameter name refuseRenamed also covers the plain-import hop refusal, which is not a rename; rename it (for example refuseDeadEnd) when this is touched. Not on the hold list: a lost edge, soundness holds.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the input gives x.g in the from-import form, matching the attribute form, red before and green after with callees pinned and the full bin delta
(b) and (c) keep their refusal; the unconditional twin follows the same rule
a mutant that restores the refusal for (a) is observed red
